answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: No, do not add a 16-miler on Wednesday. A long run three or four days out will not build any fitness that shows up by Sunday, but it will absolutely leave your legs flat on the start line. The 20 on Oct 4 and the 17 the week before are already banked, and your Wednesday marathon-pace work has been solid. The job this week is to arrive fresh, not fitter.

new.analysis:
## Reading the week

You hit every session as planned: easy days easy, the 8 with 4 at marathon pace on Wednesday, and the 12 cutdown long run. That is exactly what the first taper week should look like, and the heavy, flat legs you felt are the normal response to pulling back after the 20. It is not lost fitness.

## Why not another 16

Running 16 on Wednesday would not add fitness before Sunday; fitness gains from a long run take about ten days to show up. It would, though, leave your legs tired on race morning and shrink the glycogen tank you need. Trust the 20 on Oct 4 and the 17 the week before. That work is in the bank.

## How to race it

Target 3:45 means about 8:35/mi, and your marathon-pace reps have been sitting right there at a controlled effort. Start the first 2 miles at 8:45 to 8:50, settle into 8:35 through halfway, and only let yourself press after mile 20 if you feel strong. Carry fuel every 30 to 35 minutes from the start, and drink at every aid station once it gets warm.

## This week

Volume drops to roughly half of a normal week. The Wednesday session is short on purpose: enough faster running to keep the legs sharp, not enough to cost anything. Treat Friday and Saturday as the easiest days of the block, sleep as much as you can, and eat normally with a little extra carbohydrate from Thursday onward.
